old: Its earliest name may honor the part of your body it was built to support.
Before it meant a soft pad, its Latin ancestor named the hip or thigh.
It shares a root with coxa, the Latin word still used for the hip joint.
clues: This household item takes its name from an old Latin word for the hip, the very body part it was once meant to support.
A soft stuffed pad you sit on or lean against on a sofa, not the pillow for your head in bed. Its ending may come from a Latin word for pillow.
As a verb, it means to soften a blow, and billiard tables have rubber ones lining their edges for the balls to bounce off.
